input.model_so_far: Frame with bracket-G and bracket-H hanging on the outer middle pegs; pin-blue-E bare in the middle.

new_parts.name: fork-J
new_parts.catalog_name: Technic Pin Connector Block 3 x 3 x 1
new_parts.position: cross hole onto pin-blue-E's free axle end, hanging down between bracket-G and bracket-H

new_parts.name: knob-I
new_parts.catalog_name: Technic Pin with Friction Ridges Lengthwise and Towball
new_parts.position: pin end into fork-J's top hole, ball sticking straight up above the beam

what_each_new_part_touches: fork-J's cross hole goes onto pin-blue-E's free axle end
knob-I's pin end goes into fork-J's top hole
where_everything_is_after: fork-J: new, hanging between bracket-G and bracket-H, straddling the gap where the gear shaft will run
knob-I: new, sticking up out of the top of fork-J as a lever stud

why.problem_solved: Adds the gear-shift fork and its lever stud, so a shift lever (not in this model) can push the fork sideways to change gear.
why.why_these_parts: fork-J's slot is sized to sit in the groove of the sliding clutch sleeve built in step 9, without turning with the shaft itself.
why.sets_up_for_later: fork-J's slot will straddle the dog-clutch sleeve added in step 9, so sliding fork-J (by pushing knob-I) slides the clutch between the two gears.

review_note: fork-J's part number is a low-confidence guess -- the catalog search didn't turn up an exact match for a small red block with a vertical pin hole on top and a horizontal slot on the side; 32172 is the closest shape found (a small connector block), not a confirmed fit. Its real-machine job (gear-shift fork, straddling the clutch sleeve from step 9) is inferred from its position between bracket-G and bracket-H, exactly where the main shaft's clutch will run, and from the ball-stud on top being a standard lever-attachment point. Worth Dennis identifying the exact part from the PDF or BrickLink.
